workflow_lapses: A PowerShell pipeline was placed directly after a foreach block and failed during parsing before the closeout inventory summary ran.
A read-only ripgrep inventory supplied a Windows-invalid wildcard path and was corrected to a directory-scoped search.
The first JavaScript tool-call composer for file-size inventory had an unmatched parenthesis and did not invoke PowerShell.
The corrected composer then embedded an unescaped PowerShell backtick in a JavaScript template literal and again failed before invocation.
One read-only search named a nonexistent ariadne-continuity-graph directory before the canonical graph filename was discovered.
One PowerShell summary treated a parsed DateTime as the left operand of string concatenation and failed while formatting twelve rows.
The Windows-invalid ripgrep wildcard pattern recurred once during the API-manifest source pass before explicit directory scope was restored.
One read-only closeout-intent lookup omitted the existing closeout subdirectory and was corrected after listing the exact directory.

The first idempotent clockwork check rejected a three-parent Continuity node because the transaction schema requires exactly one active predecessor; historical Harness lineage was moved back to ordinary decision evidence.
The second idempotent clockwork check rejected five descriptive incident-stage labels outside its closed vocabulary; every row was mapped to the admitted closeout stage.
bounded_conclusion: The native Harness has enough accepted boot, tool-boundary and traceability evidence to enter monitored real work without another synthetic qualification phase. It remains a secondary worker because useful EMR4 completion is unproved. Ten cheap evidence/closeout-command lapses were corrected before publication; they caused no model, runtime, product or protected rerun and reinforce the plan to keep clockwork readings sparse.
